final.memo:
Charlie and I see a market that is exceptionally cheap by any rational standard. When we see the S&P 500 trading at less than 8 times earnings and offering an earnings yield that dwarfs the return on long-term government bonds, the logic for aggressive buying is overwhelming [D03, D04]. We are not attempting to forecast the economy or the timing of a recovery; we are simply looking at the price of business ownership relative to the cash we can expect those businesses to produce over the long term.

While the headlines are filled with talk of inflation, oil scarcity, and economic despair, we prefer to focus on the durability of the cash-generating machines we can buy today [D03, D05]. We are looking for simple, understandable businesses—utilities, newspapers, retailers—where the competitive position is secure and the management acts like owners [D01]. We have no interest in complex technological gambles or turnarounds [D01]. When stocks are on the bargain counter, we do not stand on the sidelines; we act with conviction to put our capital to work.
